reviewed_by: Claude general-purpose subagent, blind judgment reviewer, batch 1

samples_reviewed.question_text: What number comes next when counting: 62, 63, 64, 65, ___?

competency_fulfillment.rationale: The competency explicitly requires concrete and pictorial models, e.g. base-ten blocks or place-value charts, alongside numerals, but all 5 samples are either numeral-to-word conversion ('Write 57 in words.') or plain number sequences ('80, 81, 82, 83, ___'); none shows any concrete or pictorial representation.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: number_reading (1 axis/2 combos) and counting (3 axes/28 combos) together register 30 combos per variant_registry, exhaustively checked by validate_matrix separately from this illustrative 5-seed sample.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Sample sentences are all short and well under the grade-2 18-word cap, e.g. 'What number comes next when counting: 62, 63, 64, 65, ___?' is 11 words, appropriate reading demand for grade 2.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Neither of the two sampled DNAs, number_reading or counting, produced a pictorial/concrete-model item across 5 draws, so the 'variety of concrete and pictorial models' language in the competency is not evidenced in the observed variant space.

competency_alignment.rationale: The sampled skill, word-form conversion and sequence continuation, is narrower than the competency's explicit multi-representation scope of numerals plus concrete plus pictorial, so the observed content under-serves the full breadth this node claims to address.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Values observed (48-133) are a reasonable low-to-mid range appropriate as an early step toward the 1000 ceiling, so scale by itself is not the primary concern here.
